dek: Three Cuyahoga Valley waterfalls and no entrance fee. Brandywine Falls is an 86-foot drop and a short walk; Blue Hen Falls is a steep, muddy 3-mile hike.
overview: Cuyahoga Valley National Park sits between the urban edges of Cleveland and Akron, along the Cuyahoga River, deep forest and the Ohio & Erie Canal towpath.

We cover three waterfalls. Brandywine Falls is the star: USGS lists an 86-foot drop, the park's trail notes call the walk easy at about 0.3 mile round trip, and it has the most visitor reviews. Blue Hen Falls is about 3 miles round trip and described as steep, rocky and often muddy. Buttermilk Falls is in the Boston Township area of the gazetteer and has no published hike length. A fourth waterfall, Bridal Veil Falls near Bedford, falls inside the park's boundary file, but USGS places it in Bedford Reservation, so we don't count it as a park waterfall.
fallsIntro: Brandywine is the short walk. Blue Hen is the half-day hike that both the park and our notes describe as rough underfoot.
plan: For a quick visit, Brandywine Falls is about 0.3 mile round trip and the notes call it easy. Blue Hen Falls is a separate outing of about 3 miles round trip. Nothing in our sources links them into one loop, so plan them as two trips. There is no entrance gate between them, because the park doesn't charge a fee.
flow: The nearest gauge is Brandywine Creek near Macedonia (USGS 04206416), about 1.5 miles from Brandywine Falls. From 2019 through 2024 its average daily flow peaked in March at about 40 cubic feet per second and was lowest in September at about 10.

This is a rain-fed park rather than a snowmelt canyon, and the park's weather page mentions spring rain and lake-effect snow off Lake Erie. The creek rises and falls with that weather, so the peak month isn't a promise for any one day.
feesLead: There is no entrance fee and no entrance pass, so there is nothing to buy to walk to these waterfalls.
access: The Boston Mill Visitor Center sells some America the Beautiful passes, and the park says to call ahead from December through April if you need a ranger to issue one. You don't need a pass to park at Brandywine Falls or Blue Hen Falls. Brandywine is filed under Boston Heights, and Blue Hen and Buttermilk under Peninsula.
safety: Blue Hen Falls is the hike with a caution: steep, rocky and often muddy over about 3 miles round trip. Brandywine Falls is the easy one at about 0.3 mile. We have no trail warnings on file for Buttermilk Falls.
